The new equipment is expected to meet or exceed the analytical performance and configuration of the existing system, while ensuring enhanced reliability, operational stability, and long-term serviceability. The instruments will be used for advanced multi-parameter single-cell analysis and must be capable of addressing both current research needs and foreseeable future developments. The objective of this procurement is to acquire robust, high-performance analytical flow cytometry system(s), including all required hardware, software licenses, accessories, installation, user training, warranty coverage, and comprehensive service and maintenance support. The primary applications conducted by the research groups include, but are not limited to, multicolor cellular phenotyping, functional cellular assays, release assays, and related immunological and cell biology applications. The systems will be operated by experienced flow cytometry specialists as well as by a broad user community with varying levels of prior expertise. description-proc.eng: In het Aramis Project werken EBN, Gasunie, Total Energies en Shell aan het transporteren van CO₂ naar lege gascavernes op de Noordzee voor CO2-opslag. Om dit transport veilig te kunnen uitvoeren, wensen EBN en Gasunie ten behoeve van het Aramis Project diverse onderzoeken uit te voeren. Een van de benodigde onderzoeken richt zich op de reacties die in de CO₂ plaatsvinden als gevolg van verontreinigingen onder verschillende procescondities en welke gevolgen dit kan hebben voor het vormen en uittreden van zuren. EBN en Gasunie, danwel de op te richten Aramis entiteit, zijn voornemens om voor het Aramis Project een opdracht voor CO₂ laboratoriumtesten te gunnen aan het Institute for Energy Technology (IFE) zonder voorafgaande bekendmaking van een aankondiging van een opdracht. EBN en Gasunie maken hiervoor gebruik van de onderhandelingsprocedure zonder aankondiging ex artikel 2.32 lid 1 sub b onder 2 van de Aanbestedingswet. Het ontbreken van mededinging om technische redenen is gelegen in het feit dat de scope van deze opdracht dynamische stromingstesten van CO₂ samenstellingen in gasfase, cryogene vloeistoffase en hogedruk dichtfase omvat. IFE is het enige laboratorium ter wereld met aantoonbare capaciteit om dynamische stromingstesten in gas-, cryogene vloeistof- en hogedruk dichtfase en om binnen het vereiste volledige druk temperatuur¬bereik testen voor zuuruitval en corrosierisico uit te voeren. Andere laboratoria beschikken niet over de capaciteit om dynamische stromingstesten in gas-, cryogene vloeistof- en hogedruk dichtfase uit te voeren zoals door EBN en Gasunie is gewenst. Er bestaat derhalve geen redelijk alternatief of substituut en gezien de scope is het ontbreken van mededinging niet het gevolg van een kunstmatige beperking van de voorwaarden van de aanbesteding. Indien u bezwaar heeft tegen dit voornemen tot gunning dan dient u binnen 20 kalenderdagen na dagtekening van deze publicatie uw bezwaren kenbaar maken door middel van betekening aan EBN en Gasunie van een dagvaarding in kort geding voor de bevoegde voorzieningenrechter van de Rechtbank Midden-Nederland te Utrecht. Indien u na verloop van deze 20 kalenderdagen nog een rechtsvordering aanhangig maakt in verband met deze gunningsbeslissing, zullen EBN en Gasunie zich beroepen op de niet-ontvankelijkheid van uw vordering. De termijn van 20 kalenderdagen geldt derhalve als een vervaltermijn. Indien u een kort geding aanhangig maakt, dan wordt u verzocht een kopie van de conceptdagvaarding via de berichtenmodule van het platform van Mercell te sturen en voorafgaand de verhinderdata van EBN en Gasunie en hun advoca(a)t(en) bij EBN en Gasunie op te vragen.

description-proc.eng: MEDITE Europe DAC are looking for suitably qualified Fire suppression companies to install suppression systems in the following Motor Control Centre (MCC) rooms across the Medite plant. • Anner HV Sub-Station • Fire-Pump House MCC • Line1 post-press MCC Project Background Mandatory Insurance Requirement Medite electrical distribution network comprises 17 Motor Control Centre rooms, and the main HV Switch-room located at Anner Substation. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tendering process, nor does it exclude anyone from it. Details of the market dialogue are below. The Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL) is an independent state-owned expert and research institute that promotes the welfare, health and safety of the population. PRELIMINARY SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a SNOMED CT terminology management tool and related services, which will be used for producing, maintaining, and distributing Finland’s national SNOMED CT extension, reference sets (refsets), translations, and national releases. The objective is to procure a comprehensive solution that enables the following functional areas: 1) Terminology maintenance and authoring - Creation of new national concepts when the SNOMED CT International Edition does not cover national requirements. - Management of concept descriptions, synonyms, and relationships between concepts. - Logical and technical validation in accordance with SNOMED CT rules. 2) Design and management of reference sets (refsets, subsets) - Creation and maintenance of both extensional and intentional reference sets. - Version control and metadata definition for reference sets. 3) Production and management of SNOMED CT translations - Production of Finnish and Swedish terms using the translation tool. - Quality assurance and approval workflows for translations, including optional computer-assisted translation. 4) Compilation and validation of national SNOMED CT release - Assembling the national extension and all included components into a single release package. - Validation of the release according to SNOMED CT rules. - Production of publication and distribution packages in RF2 format. 5) Workflows, project management and collaboration - Task assignment, role management, approval processes, and workflow coordination. - Support for customized workflows (e.g., integration with Jira). 6) Search functions and terminology browsing - Efficient search across both the SNOMED CT International Edition and the Finnish national extension. 7) Distribution, licensing, and reporting - Distribution of the national release to various stakeholders. - Management of licensing and access control requirements. - Production of quality, translation, and validation reports. 8) Technical implementation and nonfunctional requirements - The solution shall primarily be delivered as a SaaS service, with the service provider responsible for maintenance, versioning, and technical reliability. - Browser-based user interface, APIs (API/FHIR/REST), high-level information security, usability, and scalability. - Support for multiple languages (at minimum English, Finnish and Swedish). - Integration capabilities with national code server infrastructures. The scope of work is for removal and utilization of non-hazardous and hazardous waste generated during process of construction site and waste generated by the site project area on a construction site of Poland Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) and all required waste reporting and recordkeeping activities in BDO system on behalf of Bechtel. In total approximately 37,000 Mg of waste would be generated during the period of preparatory work and approximately 137,000 Mg of waste is estimated to be generated during the construction and the commissioning period of the nuclear power plant. Companies wishing to participate in the procurement procedure must have: - the appropriate permit issued by local authorities for the disposal of liquid/solid waste, and - signed contract with a local wastewater treatment plant/solid waste landfill, or identify its key subcontractor holding such permit and contract and present them during the procurement process. Interested Companies must register/update their Contractor's information in Bechtel's iSupplier portal at https://supplier.becpsn.com link and select commodity code UB00 as their specialty. If Contractor has any questions or intends to express interest in bidding this requirement, the Company shall notify Bechtel’s Contact Person. At that point, Bechtel shall provide the interested party the Poland Prequalification Questionnaire which Company would complete with response to Bechtel for review. Bechtel notes that previous proven experience with trash services of similar scale and complexity will be mandatory and providing additional documentation / evidence of previous experience may be required. The prequalification questionnaire includes a list of questions required to be considered as prequalified, and examples to include demonstration of (i) experience in providing the trash services in the past or current projects, (ii) safety record and compliance to quality requirements (see section 7),(iii) compliance to certification of legally mandatory requirements (including anti-corruption and sanctions), (iv) financial standing (solvency), and (v) organizational capabilities. In the event of high competitiveness of the proceedings (a large number of companies expressing interest), Bechtel reserves the right to conduct a preliminary preselection of companies for further proceedings, which demonstrate the greatest potential for performing the scope of work. Upon Bechtel’s evaluation of a response to the Poland Prequalification Questionnaire, Bechtel will notify if the Company meets, conditionally meets, or does not meet the prequalification requirements that closely match the requirements. A Company's submission of Prequalification Questionnaire does not automatically qualify the Company to be a pre-qualified Company. Bechtel reserves the right to exclude any of the following from this Competitive Bidding process: a. any economic operator that is directly or indirectly owned or controlled by an entity from a country not covered by the Government Procurement Agreement ("GPA") with the EU; or b. economic operators who rely in the Competitive Bidding process on capacities of any entities from countries not covered by the GPA with the EU. Such decision of Bechtel shall not be subject to complaint. Each prequalified Company will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). Companies meeting the prequalification criteria and who have executed the NDA will be invited to submit the proposals for trash services. The Request for Quotation (RFQ) shall include the award criteria, scope of work, specifications, drawings, datasheets, terms and conditions, and schedule data. The RFQ shall be issued via Bechtel’s Digital Supply Chain System automation tool. The RFQ document will include the scope of services on the Poland AP1000 Project. The Company is responsible for providing fully qualified personnel to perform trash services. Additionally, the company shall provide uniforms and equipment in accordance to scope of work. The Company is required to have: • ISO 9001 or equivalent • ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 • Seller’s activities will need to comply with Polish Law and National Standards. Proposals may be provided in either EURO or PLN or USD. Furthermore, the proposals will be requested as a combination of lump sum items and fixed unit rate items. Award criteria shall be based on a combination of the highest evaluated scored bidder with consideration of the following key criteria in order of relevance, together with cost, which will determine the final decision for award which will be detailed further in the Bid Document(s) and during the RFQ phase. a. Technical Capability b. Previous Proven Relevant Experience c. Environmental Health and Safety Performance The Customer shall be responsible for monitoring the Contractor’s compliance with the competitive procedure. description-proc.eng: With this request for information, HUS launches a market consultation to prepare a procurement. The aim of this prior information notice is to find suppliers operating in this field of business, get information of the solutions available in the market, and inform our plans and requirements for any possible forthcoming procurement. Suppliers are requested to consult the information and questions of the RFI and to deliver their responses according to the instructions below. SUBJECT OF PROCUREMENT The subject of procurement is: HUS Pediatric Sleep Laboratory is looking to procure two (2) new PSG (Polysomnography) devices suitable for pediatric sleep laboratory use. The ones currently in use are set to be renewed. Within their answer respondents are encouraged to also attach any and all of the following available of the products/services: - Brochures - Technical specifications - User manuals - Price estimates / price lists - Periodic maintenance plan (need for scheduled maintenance, who performs it and the cost estimate) - SpO2 measurement technology used in the system (e.g. Nonin, Masimo) - System specific consumables and their prices - Price of a possible on site installation visit, based on a two day installation period - Any other relevant information The PSG system must be capable of measuring at least the following signals. Please provide at least a YES/NO answer to each requirement with optional elaborations. 1. EEG 2. EOG 3. Submental EMG 4. Diaphragmatic EMG 5. ECG 6. Respiratory airflow (pressure and thermistor) 7. Respiratory effort (thorax and abdomen, RIP technology) 8. Oxygen saturation (SpO2), pulse, and plethysmogram 9. Body position 10. Video recording synchronized with physiological signals In addition, the system must meet the following criteria: - The system can be used for PSG studies in patients of all ages, starting from newborns (excluding premature infants). - The system is wireless. - Signals produced by external measurement devices can be integrated into the PSG recording when needed and are visible in real time during data acquisition. (Examples of external measurement devices are Sentec SDM and Medlab cap10. It should be possible to integrate parameters from respiratory support devices on demand, too.) - The system supports ambulatory PSG recordings, for example in a hospital ward or in a care facility. - The system can calculate a non invasive, continuous blood pressure estimate using pulse transit time (PTT). - The analysis software includes an ECG artifact removal algorithm, applicable at least to the diaphragmatic EMG signal. - The analysis software supports drift correction for the Sentec signal. - The analysis software allows export of signals with timestamps in CSV or TXT format. - The analysis software allows export of events and analyses (including sleep stages, apneas, hypopneas, desaturations, and arousals) with timestamps. - A network license or other flexible licensing solution is available for the analysis software. The software is used on 25-35 different workstations, with a maximum of 6 simultaneous users. - Shared analysis settings can be defined for all users, and deployment of these settings across all analysis workstations does not require user action. ANSWERING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Answers to questions below should be submitted by 28.4.2026 12:00 GMT+2 at the latest to the email address: kilpailutus.diagnostiikka@hus.fi. The title or message field of the e-mail should mention: HUS 194-2026 PSG Equipment for a Pediatric Sleep Laboratory This notice is not a call for tenders. HUS may specify the subject of the procurement in a subsequent contract notice. The requirements for a subsequent procurement and invitation to tender will be determined on the basis of the needs of the contracting entity, with the aim of taking into account the information obtained in the market survey. This notice provides the information currently held by the contracting entity on the procurement to operators on the market. The procurement is in the planning stage and the plans, with their schedules and information, can still be specified and changed. The request for information does not oblige the procurement unit to carry out the actual procurement, but the decision to initiate a possible procurement process is made separately. Neither the request for information nor its replies are binding on either party. Responding to a request for information does not affect the position of the tenderer in the forthcoming tender. The costs associated with responding to a request for information are borne by the respondent, and HUS does not pay compensation for responding to a request for information or participating the procurement procedure.

DTU has an 18-year-old hydrogen generator that needs replacement. It produces hydrogen gas based on electrolysis of ultra-pure water. The preferred hydrogen generator type for ultra-pure semiconductor fabrication is the one based on electrolysis of ultra-pure water. This rules out generator types using other electrolytes. The capacity requirement is 60 normal liters of hydrogen per minute at 15 Bars. The consumption is not constant in time, so the system should be able to adjust hydrogen production according to the demand. DTU has searched the market for hydrogen generators with ultra-pure water as electrolyte and only found two suppliers with the capability and capacity described in the description above: • LNI Swissgas GmbH in Germany • Nel Hydrogen in USA There will be a saving of choosing a Hydrogen Generator from LNI Swiss gas. Furthermore, in the present geopolitical situation, it is deemed logistically and economically safer to purchase a European tool with respect to e.g. post-sale service, shipment of spare parts and sudden extra import customs. Hence, there is only one supplier due to technical reasons.

title-proc.eng: Textiles from 6 recycling stations

description-proc.eng: Background The waste management company for Drammensregionen IKS (RfD) receives increasing quantities of textiles at its recycling stations. At the same time the market for sorting and further handling textiles is changing, with varying capacity, requirements and price level. In order to ensure predictable operation and good use of resources, RfD needs a robust, long-term and traceable system for handling textiles. The procurement is being carried out in order to safeguard RfD ́s responsibility in accordance with the Waste Regulations § 10a-4 letter f), and to contribute to the textiles as far as possible going to reuse and recycling. The need for documentation and control in the value chain is sharpened, and RfD would like a system that provides a better overview of fractions and treatment routes, as well as reduces the risk of undesired handling and a lack of traceability. Furthermore, there is a need for reliable collection at the recycling stations, including handling variations and periods with peak load, so that the reception systems are not crowded and that the public experiences an available and orderly tender offer. Description of the assignment RfD shall enter into an agreement with one tenderer for the collection, sorting and further handling of textiles from six recycling stations. The estimated annual volume is approx. 500 tonnes, with expected variations throughout the year. The assignment includes logistics from the recycling stations to the tenderer ́s reception, as well as sorting and distribution to further treatment systems. The delivery shall support high operational security, including ability to handle peak loads and contribute to the prevention of crowded collection systems, for example through planning based on data on the filling degree. The textiles shall be handled in accordance with the waste hierarchy, with the aim that as much as possible go into reuse, then material recovery and any energy recovery. Tenderers shall submit relevant documentation on the route of treatment and amounts, as well as ensure traceability and seriousness in the entire value chain, including any sub-suppliers and recipients. RfD provides communication with households for the delivery of textiles. Sub-contracts We follow the Norwegian Environment Agency ́s municipal supervisor on sorting. It says that "The textiles can be source sorted into three streams". We therefore have 3 sub-contracts. Tenderers can participate in only re-use or textile waste or "wet and dirty". Tenderers can participate in one, two or all three. The price or "not participating" shall be completed in the price form. The evaluation of sub-contracts will be based on the same award criteria independent of sub-contract, with the exception of price. All criteria connected to the environment and quality are general and independent of fraction. The contracting authority will assess whether sub-contracts will be signed or not.
